title.narrative: MAURITANIA - Basic Education Sector Support Project - Phase 2

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective is to improve the quality of primary education and service delivery in Selected Regions.

The objective of the Second Phase of the Basic Education Sector Support Project for Mauritania is to improve the quality of primary education and service delivery in Selected Regions. The project has four components. (1) Transforming teacher management using accountability frameworks and new technology component will focus on: (i) improving the quality of teaching and learning in primary schools, through a strengthened pre-service teacher training to improve the quality of the flow of teachers; (ii) strengthening teacher management and professional development to improve the quality of the stock of teachers; (iii) establishing a strategic staffing mechanism to move low performing teachers out of the classrooms; and (iv) introducing scripted lessons in primary school classrooms. It will also have a strong gender focus and several activities can take place beyond the selected regions. (2) Improving education service delivery in selected regions component seeks to improve inclusion and social cohesion via primary schools in the six selected regions. The financing will improve the delivery of education services through better allocation of resources and enhanced school-based management. The component will support the implementation of a new sector management model that streamlines and simplifies the interaction between central, regional, and sub-regional levels to efficiently allocate scarce resources to schools across and within the regions. (3) Strengthening the management of the education sector component will focus on: (i) building capacity for managers of the education sector at the central, regional, and district level; (ii) supporting all levels in setting up and maintaining strong information systems; (iii) supporting regional and district levels to fulfill their supervision role of schools; and (iv) supporting project management and monitoring and evaluation (M&E). (4) Contingent Emergency Response Component will be included under the proposed project in accordance with the World Bank Investment Project Financing (IPF) Policy to help the Government improve the response time if a crisis occurs and urgent assistance is needed. The CERC allows for rapid reallocation of project proceeds in the event of a future natural or man-made disaster or crisis that has caused or is likely imminently to cause a major adverse economic and/or social impact. This component will have no funding allocation initially. In the event of a future emergency, the Government could activate the CERC and request the World Bank's approval to recategorize and reallocate financing from uncommitted resources to cover emergency response and recovery costs.

condition.narrative: Not later than four (4) months after the Effective Date or any later date agreed upon in writing with the Association, theRecipient, through MENFTR, shall recruit or assign to the Project: (i) an internal auditor; and (ii) an external auditor; both withterms of reference, qualifications and experience satisfactory to the Association.

The Manuals of Procedures shall include: (i) a manual for the design and implementation of ENIs educational projects; (ii) a manualfor the operationalization of COGES, as well as the design and implementation of the school implementation plans and the managementof School Grants; (iii) a manual for the design and implementation of the RDPs; and (iv) a financial management manual to clarifyroles and responsibilities of all stakeholders, including School Grants beneficiaries, the latter which shall be adopted by theRecipient in form and substance satisfactory to the Association no later than four (4) months after the Effective Date, or anylater date agreed upon in writing with the Association.

The Recipient shall ensure at all times during Project implementation after January 1, 2023, or any other date agreed upon inwriting with the Association, that the CNE in charge of the administration and evaluation of primary school teachers underComponent 1 of the Project is staffed with sufficient and adequate personnel, and the necessary resources to carry out the relevantactivities to be implemented under the Project.

The Recipient shall establish, not later than two (2) months after the effective date, and thereafter maintain, throughout theProject implementation period with composition, mandate, and resources satisfactory to the Association, a Steering Committee, to bechaired by representative of the Minister of MENFTR, the DSPC shall serve as its secretary, and it shall further be comprised of,inter alia, representatives of the Recipient's Ministry of Economic Affairs and the Promotion of Productive Sectors; Ministry ofCivil Service; as well as, a representative of the ENIs. The Steering Committee shall also include, as observers, representativesof IDENs and DRENs; civil society; and teachers unions.

The Recipient shall no later than two (2) months after the Effective Date recruit and maintain throughout Project implementation: aProject coordinator; a component-specific technical coordinator for each Components 1 and 2 of the Project; a financial managementspecialist; a procurement specialist; a monitoring and evaluation specialist; a construction manager; an environmental safeguardsspecialist; a social safeguards specialist; a communications and citizen engagement specialist; an accountant; and assistants asneeded; all with qualifications, terms of reference and experience acceptable to the Association.

title.narrative: Share of ENI graduates who attain the desired level to teach

comment.narrative: ENI would-be graduates in their third year will be tested with a standardized exit exam. The students will be classified into four groups: (i) weak, form those considered not ready to teach; (ii) insufficient, for those who have serious deficiencies and a slim chance of being upskilled; (iii) average, for those who can be brought up to standard with some adequate additional training; and (iv) desired, for those who have the pre-requisite to become teachers. The classification is consistent with that of Decree 2019-040/P.M/M.E.N.F.P on the evaluation of teachers.
